You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 51f9b6450e848023d1996e0762e92e388a598239 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Janik Kleinhoff <janik@kleinhoff.de>
Date: Tue, 30 Dec 2014 12:31:45 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] operserv/akill: fix crash bug introduced in a2126db3

/os AKILL ADD would segfault as it'd try to compare the non-existent
first argument to "FORCE".
---
 modules/operserv/akill.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/modules/operserv/akill.c b/modules/operserv/akill.c
index 0db7d58a7..e26841afc 100644
--- a/modules/operserv/akill.c
+++ b/modules/operserv/akill.c
@@ -126,7 +126,7 @@ static void os_cmd_akill_add(sourceinfo_t *si, int parc, char *parv[])
 	char *s;
 	kline_t *k;
 
-	if (!strcasecmp(token, "FORCE"))
+	if (token && !strcasecmp(token, "FORCE"))
 	{
 		if (has_priv(si, PRIV_AKILL_ANYMASK))
 		{
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a null pointer dereference when the `token` variable was not initialized or was set to NULL. The code attempted to compare this non-existent first argument to the string "FORCE", leading to a segmentation fault (segfault). The patch added a check to ensure that `token` is not NULL before performing the comparison, thus preventing the crash.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a null pointer dereference when the `token` variable was not initialized or was set to NULL. The code attempted to compare this non-existent first argument to the string "FORCE", leading to a segmentation fault (segfault). The patch added a check to ensure that `token` is not NULL before performing the comparison, thus preventing the crash.
